utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Madam Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Case Number IT-98-33-A, The Prosecutor versus Radislav Krstic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a Status Conference called pursuant to Rule 65 bis. Judge hunt who served as the Pre-appeal Judge in this case has been replaced on the Bench for this case, so I will be presiding today. Let me first ask for appearances. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Prosecution is Norman Farrell, Mr. Mathias Marcussen, and Ms. Nicola Bonfield. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Nenad Petrusic joined here today by Mr. Norman Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. General Krstic, please do not feel you have to stand when I address you. Please remain seated if you prefer. Are you able to follow the proceedings in a language that you understand? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me note the parties should be aware by now that the Appeals Chamber yesterday granted the Defence request for an extension of time until the 7th of August to file supplementary Rule 115 materials based on the interviews mentioned in the request. I can also report that I am hopeful that the Appeals Chamber will render a decision on the Defence's pending Rule 115 motions quite soon. Let me also say at the very outset that while I'm grateful to the parties for their professional conduct, I do hope that both sides will redouble their efforts to move this appeal forward. The Prosecution, of course, must diligently fulfill its disclosure obligations, and the Defence must have adequate time to scrutinise whatever it receives from the Prosecution. But I hope that both sides will carry out their responsibilities with a sense of urgency. Mr. Farrell, thank you very much for the status report filed on Monday. I would like to ask you a few questions about it if I may, and then I will let you supplement whatever you would want. Now, the first two groups of documents mentioned in your annex concern, as you remember, interviews with three individuals. Are those interviews now completed; and if not, when do you expect them to be completed? In other words, when should disclosures resulting from these interviews be done with?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: First of all, I understand that there is continuing, ongoing investigations in relation to a few of the individuals listed in the disclosure as a result, as you know, there are other trials that are ongoing. At this point in time, there is no -- there are no other interviews that have taken place, though I understand that there may be efforts to continue in relation to one or two of the individuals. At this point in time, there is no further material to be disclosed in relation to those individuals, but I will certainly inform the Defence counsel, and if the Court so wishes, if and when those matters arise. And of course as soon as they're completed, they will be disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Farrell. Now I'm turning to the third item in your annex. I'm wondering why did it take two months from the testimony in question until the disclosure of the material to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: I'm take responsibility for that. Mr. -- I think it was at the end of May, in fact, the Defence wrote to us asking about that issue. It got overlooked for a period of time in light of other obligations. That's our responsibility. That's not the responsibility of the Defence. They wrote, and we had conversations about that. And then they were subsequently reviewed. That was -- well, there was a number of other things that we were doing at the time, and we wanted to review the transcript because of the sensitivity of it, but the length of time is primarily the responsibility of my Office and I'll certainly take note of that in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farrell.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I turn now to the fourth set of material in your annex. I see you have already disclosed a number of documents. Do you know when you will be completed with your review of this entire set of documents, and thus when will you be finished with the disclosures to the Defence from this particular group of documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: I think I can inform you, Your Honour, and I'll allow of course my learned colleagues to speak. We had an opportunity to meet, counsel for General Krstic and counsel for the Prosecution yesterday afternoon to go through some of these issues. We have informed the counsel for General Krstic that we would attempt to by the end of day provide a CD of the remaining materials, that is, the fourth one, the MUP and related intelligence documents that have been seized. Mr. Marcussen and I reviewed it this morning. We haven't been able to separate out all the relevant from the irrelevant material, but we've undertaken to the Defence that we will provide it within the next day or two and we will provide it on CD. I hoped to provide it today, but we're not able to. But I will provide it to them so they can actually search it electronically. I get in the next day or two, we will get it to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: The electronic search did not seem to present any problems for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Not as yet. If it is, I will allow them to inform us, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I will now turn to paragraph 6 of your status report. You mentioned one document that you anticipated disclosing to the Defence by the time of the Status Conference. Have you done so?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It was done yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Finally, in the last paragraph of your status report, you referred to ongoing investigations that may lead to further disclosure to the Defence. Are there any investigations or episodes of testimony in other cases you are aware of other than the ones mentioned in the annex to your report? And related to that, can you anticipate when the disclosure to the Defence in this case will be finally completed?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: To answer your last question first, if I may, unfortunately I don't think it would be possible to maybe ever indicate if there's a completion of the disclosure. As I indicated in my meeting with the Defence yesterday, the other cases that relate to the area of Srebrenica, as you know, are in the case of Mr. Blagojevic and also in the case of Mr. Milosevic. Those cases, as you're fully aware, Mr. President, are ongoing. And as a result of matters that arise in those cases, the Prosecution is attempting to review the material that comes in, continue any follow-up investigations or investigate any issues that the Defence raises in those cases. The purpose of the last passage in paragraph 6 was to inform you, which I'm fully aware of, that you and the Defence are apprised of this matter, but there is ongoing cases that address the same -- exact same region, and therefore if there is anything that arises from those, they will be disclosed. The second part of your question was is there any ongoing investigations now? As far as I'm aware, besides the one that I mentioned in relation to the persons listed in the disclosure report, as far as -- I'm not aware of any other information at the moment that is presently in our possession or has come in as a result of the investigations, though I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. do know that in fact the investigations in those two cases are ongoing. It has been our position that as soon as it comes in, we will disclose it as soon as possible. But as far as the Prosecution is concerned, we will set a date and proceed with the matter. As things come in we'll apprise you and, of course, disclose to the Defence immediately any issues that arise. But as far as the material we have, we're ready to proceed. The material that we have is continually being disclosed. And as it comes in, I presume it's not Your Honour's intention - certainly not ours - to postpone until the end of those trials, so we will continue on that basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farrell. I'm sure, or at least I like to hope, that everybody here is united in the desire to move this case forward and to come hopefully to hearings before long.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Now I will -- is there anything else you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Not on behalf of the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then I will turn to the Defence, and I would like to ask a few questions. In paragraph 5 of its status report, the Prosecution indicates that there are two individuals the Defence is still seeking to interview. Their identities, of course, must be kept confidential. Are you still seeking to interview these individuals, and if so, what have you, counsel for the Defence, done in that regard?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: The answer is yes, Your Honour, we are still seeking to interview these two individuals. And Mr. Petrusic has made very diligent efforts over the last few months to interview these folks. And to this date has been unsuccessful. Mr. Petrusic is going to try again this coming week to interview these folks voluntarily. We realise that under the now recent decision of the Court we do have the power that we can request the Court to issue subpoenas. We would like to avoid that if possible. We know how difficult that procedure is, and how cumbersome it is. When I say cumbersome it's no reflection on the Tribunal; it simply takes time and effort. So if we can accomplish that in the next week, we will. If we can't, we may reluctantly have to ask the assistance of the Tribunal in issuing subpoenas to these two individuals. We're hoping that we can do it without that, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I appreciate your efforts to proceed on your own power, if I may. If I do need the assistance of the Appeals Chamber, you know where to turn.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Now, and my second question is do you expect to file any more 115 motions? And if so, could we get an indication of when would this be done?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: We think we will, Your Honour. If the two interviews -- by the way, there's one other interview, which in the interest of confidentiality, I'm sure the Prosecution would agree with this, one other gentleman who we're going to seek to interview. And we do believe that either in that material or in material still to be disclosed by the Prosecution, there will be a basis for a further motion because Mr. Farrell himself acknowledges that in the material that's going to be turned over to us, there's undoubtedly some Rule 68 materials. So -- in an abundance of caution, rather than say we're not going to, my best judgement, Your Honour, is we are going to file an addition supplemental Rule 115 motion. Of course, we know Your Honour's desire and the Chamber's desire to move this case along, and truly we do share that. And we will be filing that motion just as soon as we possibly can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, counsel. Is there anything else that the Defence would like to raise in today's status conference?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I don't think so, Your Honour. There is one matter, and we raised this before Judge Hunt. General Krstic had his leg amputated some years ago and has had problems since. He had an operation some time ago by a Dutch surgeon, and at the last Status Conference in March we asked the Judge if he might lend the assistance of the Tribunal and the Registry to have that surgeon visit the General Krstic. We thought that may have -- was done, but apparently it wasn't. So I just wanted to inform Your Honour that today, I sent a letter to Timothy McFadden at the Detention Centre a personal letter from General Krstic with a cover letter from me asking Mr. McFadden to have the same Dutch surgeon who accomplished that operation come to see General Krstic because he is in continual pain, and I realise that you're not in this business, Your Honour, I mention it to you because we're a little disappointed that nothing was done following the March Status Conference. And so I'm simply noting it for Your Honour. Hopefully within the next few weeks that situation will be remedied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, thank you. And I really think you did the right thing by raising this matter with me. I am very much concerned about the continuing health problems, infections or whatever, that General Krstic has suffering from. And I would appreciate it if the Registrar, Madam Registrar, if you would inform the people concerned, that I would like to have a report why nothing has been done that since the Status Conference that my distinguished colleague, Judge Hunt, conducted. I read the transcript of that conference, so I am well aware of the problem. I have also assumed that the problem has been addressed. Well, if there is nothing else that either the Defence or the Prosecution would want to raise, let me just say that I am grateful to the parties for their attendance, and this Status Conference is adjourned.
